Class MacHWDiskStore

java.lang.Object
oshi.hardware.common.AbstractHWDiskStore
oshi.hardware.common.platform.mac.MacHWDiskStore
All Implemented Interfaces:
HWDiskStore
@ThreadSafe public abstract class MacHWDiskStore extends AbstractHWDiskStore
Base class for macOS HWDiskStore implementations. Subclasses provide platform-specific disk enumeration and statistics updates.

      protected MacHWDiskStore(String name, String model, String serial, long size, String diskType, Optional<List<String>> backingStores)
      Creates a MacHWDiskStore built on other storage. A disk with at least one backing store, such as an APFS container or a disk image, is typed Virtual whatever its media reports.
      Parameters:
      name - the disk name
      model - the disk model
      serial - the serial number
      size - the disk size in bytes
      diskType - the disk type its media reports
      backingStores - the stores this disk is built on, or empty if they could not be read

  • Method Details

    • getBackingStores

      public Optional<List<String>> getBackingStores()
      Description copied from interface: HWDiskStore
      The stores this disk is built on, when it is a layer over other storage rather than a device in its own right.

      A layered disk is listed alongside the stores it is built on, so its capacity and I/O statistics duplicate theirs. This is the case for a device-mapper (LVM, LUKS, multipath) or md RAID device on Linux, an APFS container or a disk image on macOS, and a Storage Spaces or file-backed virtual disk on Windows.

      An empty Optional means the backing stores are not reported, either because the platform does not report them or because they could not be read, and says nothing about whether the disk is layered. A present but empty list means the disk is not built on anything OSHI can see. Summing the I/O of only the disks whose result is present and empty therefore counts each transfer once, provided every disk's result is present and every store it names is itself listed. Windows does not list the physical disks of a Storage Spaces pool, so there the Storage Spaces disk is the only entry carrying their transfers.

      Backing stores are reported on Linux, from each block device's sysfs slaves directory; on macOS, from the IOKit registry; and on Windows 8 and Server 2012 or later, from the Storage namespace of WMI. Other platforms return an empty Optional.

      Each entry is a HWDiskStore.StoreKind prefix followed by a name that matches a getter on the corresponding class:

      Backing store entries
      Kind Name matches Examples
      HWDiskStore.StoreKind.DISK HWDiskStore.getName() disk:/dev/sda, disk:\\.\PHYSICALDRIVE1
      HWDiskStore.StoreKind.PARTITION HWPartition.getIdentification() partition:/dev/sda2, partition:disk0s2
      HWDiskStore.StoreKind.FILE OSFileStore.getMount() of the file store holding the backing file file:/System/Volumes/Data, file:C:\
      An entry may name a store that is not in the current list, such as a network file store when only local file stores were requested.
      Returns:
      An Optional containing the stores this disk is built on, sorted, which is an empty list for a disk that is not layered; or empty if the backing stores are not reported.

    • mediaBackingStore

      protected static Optional<List<String>> mediaBackingStore(@Nullable String bsdName, @Nullable Boolean whole)
      Builds the backing store of a disk whose nearest IOMedia ancestor in the IOService plane is another media object: the partition an APFS container is synthesized on, or the disk it is carved from.
      Parameters:
      bsdName - the ancestor's BSD Name, or null if it has none
      whole - the ancestor's Whole property, or null if absent
      Returns:
      the backing store, or empty if the ancestor has no BSD name

    • imageBackingStore

      protected static Optional<List<String>> imageBackingStore(String imageUrl, UnaryOperator<String> mountOf)
      Builds the backing store of a disk image: the file store holding the image file.
      Parameters:
      imageUrl - the image device's DiskImageURL
      mountOf - returns the mount point of the file store holding a path, or an empty string if it cannot be read
      Returns:
      the backing store, or empty if the image is not a local file or its file store could not be read
